title: The Tenants page and tenant details drawer in the Identities menu: list columns, views, drawer tabs and which tenants are shown

prose.text: {{page-scope}} Whether an Inactive tenant is ever shown differs between sentences {{divergence:inactive-state}}; what makes a tenant Inactive is open {{gap:inactive-tenants}}. {{page-summaries}} {{page-actions}}

prose.label: The list.
prose.text: {{list-columns}} How Next Scan relates to the AD and Entra ID scan schedules is open {{gap:scan-schedule}}.

checks.do: Whether the tenant being asked about is Active, since the page text says only tenants in an active state are displayed.

page-scope.statement: The Tenants page (Identities > Tenants) lists tenant accounts and their identities with identity findings per tenant, and the page text says only tenants in an active state are displayed.

quotes: You can view a consolidated list of tenant accounts and their identities on the Tenants page.
Only tenants in an active state are displayed on the Tenants page.
On the Tenants page (Identities > Tenants), you can do the following:
You can also review the identity findings for each tenant and the total number of critical or high-severity findings

page-summaries.statement: The Tenants page shows the number of tenants grouped by severity level (for example Critical, High, Medium, Low), the total identity findings across all tenants, and the total active identity providers with identity findings.

quotes: View the number of tenants grouped by severity level (e.g., Critical, High, Medium, and Low).
View the total identity findings across all tenants.
View the total active identity providers with identity findings.

page-actions.statement: The Tenants page supports system-saved and user-saved views, search, saved current view, filters, grouping (for example by Tenant First Seen, Tenant Last Seen, Tenant Tags), refresh, a CSV export of tenants and their details, and column changes.

quotes: Select from system-saved views or views you previously saved.
Group tenants by category (e.g., Tenant First Seen, Tenant Last Seen, Tenant Tags, etc).
Export the list of tenants and their associated details as a CSV file.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Search for a tenant.
Save the current view.
Apply filters to view specific information.
Refresh the table to reflect the most current information.

list-columns.statement: The tenant list shows ID, Name, Severity Score, Total Identity Findings (critical, high, medium and low), Sources (an ITDR feed, for example ITDR Change Detection AD, ITDR Domains AD), Last Seen, State (Active or Inactive), Identity Provider (for example AD, Entra ID) and Next Scan.

quotes: Severity Score: The severity score of the tenant.
Total Identity Findings: The total number of critical, high, medium, and low identity findings for the tenant.
Sources: The source of the identity finding (e.g., ITDR Change Detection AD, ITDR Domains AD, etc.).
Last Seen: The date of the most recent activity.
State: The state of the tenant's account (Active or Inactive).
Identity Provider: The identity provider configured for the tenant (e.g., AD, Entra ID, etc.).
Next Scan: The date and time of the next scan for a data sync.
ID: The unique identifier of the tenant.
Name: The name of the tenant.

details-tab.statement: The tenant details drawer's Details tab shows Tenant ID, Last Scan (date and time of the last scan for a data sync), Scan Frequency (for example Daily, Weekly), icons whose source is shown on hover, and the total of Critical, High, Medium and Low identity findings.

quotes: Tenant ID: The unique identifier of the tenant.
Last Scan: The date and time of the last scan for a data sync.
Scan Frequency: The frequency of the scan (e.g., Daily, Weekly, etc.).
Hover over each icon to view the source.
Identity Findings: The total number of Critical, High, Medium, and Low identity findings for the tenant.

findings-tab.statement: The tenant drawer's Identity Findings tab lists findings with Severity (Critical and High are prioritized), Name, Type of Risk (for example Kerberos Abuse, Account Management, Credential Exposure), MITRE Tactics and MITRE Techniques, and can be exported to CSV.

quotes: Severity: The severity level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low). The Critical and High severity findings are prioritized.
Type of Risk: The type of risk (e.g., Kerberos Abuse, Account Management, Credential Exposure, etc.).
MITRE Tactics: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic ID.
MITRE Techniques: The MITRE ATT&CK technique that the adversary used.
Click the Export as CSV icon to export the identity findings list for a tenant to a CSV file.
Name: The name of the identity finding.

identities-tab.statement: The tenant drawer's Identities tab shows each identity's Name, Identity Type (User, Service Principal, or Special Identities), Is Admin (true if the user is an admin) and Type (Internal or External).

quotes: Name: The name of the user.
Identity Type: The type of identity (User, Service Principal, or Special Identities).
Is Admin: The user's admin role status. If the user is an admin, this field shows true.
Type: The type of user (Internal or External).

mitre-tab.statement: The tenant drawer's MITRE ATT&CK tab shows the tenant's identity findings categorized in MITRE ATT&CK tactics, with a Read more icon on hover that opens the MITRE tactics web page.

quotes: On the MITRE ATT&CK tab, you can view the identity findings categorized in MITRE ATT&CK tactics.
Hover over the tactic to see the Read more icon, and click the icon to go to the MITRE tactics web page.

inactive-state.summary: The Tenants page says only tenants in an active state are displayed, while its State column is described as Active or Inactive.

positions.says: Only tenants in an active state are displayed on the Tenants page.

quotes: Only tenants in an active state are displayed on the Tenants page.

positions.says: The State column is the state of the tenant's account (Active or Inactive).

quotes: State: The state of the tenant's account (Active or Inactive).

inactive-state.impact: An answer saying whether an Inactive tenant appears in the list depends on which sentence is followed.

inactive-tenants.title: What makes a tenant Inactive and whether an Inactive tenant is ever displayed
inactive-tenants.detail: The Tenants page says only tenants in an active state are displayed, while its State column is described as Active or Inactive. The captured pages do not say what makes a tenant Inactive or whether the State value Inactive can appear.

scan-schedule.title: How Scan Frequency and Next Scan relate to the AD and Entra ID scan schedules, and which values exist
scan-schedule.detail: The tenant pages give Scan Frequency only as 'e.g., Daily, Weekly, etc.' and define Next Scan as the date and time of the next scan for a data sync; they do not say how this relates to the Daily, Weekly, Monthly and Quarterly schedule lists in identity-protection.entra-connection and identity-protection.posture-scans, or which values exist. Roles and permissions needed to view tenants are also not stated.
